sentences.text:
By way of filing this Criminal Revision Petition challenge has been made to the judgment dated 28.11.2003 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge No.2, Chittorgarh in Criminal appeal No.20/2002, whereby the learned appellate court affirmed the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 02.11.2002 passed by the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kapasan,
Chittorgarh in Criminal Regular Case No.08/1995; whereby the petitioner has been convicted for the offence under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentenced to suffer six months' of rigorous imprisonment along with fine of Rs. 1000/- and in default of payment of fine,
further to undergo one month simple imprisonment.
2.

Bereft of elaborate details, facts relevant and essential for disposal of the instant criminal revision petition are that the Food (2 of 5) [CRLR-1119/2003] Inspector Labh Shankar Bohra on 16.05.1993 at around 08:00 a.m. reached the shop of the petitioner where he was selling milk which was stored in a container.

Upon suspicion, the food inspector took sample of the milk from the accused-petitioner after following the due procedure and sent the same for analysis to public analyst who gave a report Ex. P-12. Finding the same to be adulterated.
Thus, after obtaining prosecution sanction, a complaint was submitted against the petitioner in the competent court for the offence under Section 7/16 of the PFA Act.
The learned magistrate summoned the accused and after hearing on charge, framed charge against him for the aforesaid offence, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

After conducting a full-fledged trial, the learned trial court convicted and sentenced Mohan Lal vs State on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82421576/
1 the petitioner in the manner stated above vide judgment dated 02.11.2002.

sentences.text: The appeal preferred against the aforesaid judgment was dismissed by the learned appellate court vide judgment dated 28.11.2003 while affirming the conviction and maintaining the sentence awarded to the petitioner.
Hence, this revision petition is preferred by him.

3. After arguing the case on merits to some extent, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that he will not assail conviction of the petitioners and confine his arguments to the alternative prayer of reduction of the sentence awarded by the trial court.

He submits that there is non-compliance of Section 13(2) of PF Act as one sample was sent for analysis to laboratory at Udaipur and another was sent to the laboratory at Pratapgarh and the report was not supplied to the petitioner which is mandate (3 of 5) [CRLR-1119/2003] of law.
He submits that the incident in the present case pertains to the year 1993.
The petitioner was 33 years of age at the time of incident and presently, he is aged 63 years.
The petitioner has already suffered agony of protracted trial for long 30 years.
He was not having any criminal antecedents and it was the first criminal case registered against him.
No adverse remark has been passed over his conduct except the impugned judgment.
The petitioner has remained in custody for sometime during the trial as well as after passing of judgment of appeal.
No fruitful purpose would be served by sending the present petitioner to jail at this stage.
With these submissions, learned counsel prays that by taking a lenient view, the sentence awarded to the petitioner may be reduced to the period already undergone by him.

4. Learned public prosecutor has, of course, been able to defend the case on merits but does not refute the fact that the petitioner has remained behind the bars for some time and the case is pending since long.

5. Since the revision petition against conviction is not pressed and after perusing the material,
nothing is noticed which requires interference in the finding of guilt reached by learned trial court and affirmed by the appellate court, this court does not wish to interfere in the judgment of conviction.
Accordingly, the judgment of conviction is maintained.
6. As far as the question of quantum of sentence in concerned, it is worthwhile to note that the occurrence in this case pertains to the year 1993.
The petitioner was 33 years of age at the time of incident and presently, he is aged 63 years.
The right to speedy (4 of 5) [CRLR-1119/2003] and expeditious trial is one of the most valuable and cherished rights guaranteed under the Constitution.
It was the first criminal case registered against him.
He has not been shown to be indulged in any other criminal case except this one.
He remained incarcerated for some days after passing of the judgment in appeal.
The petitioner has already suffered the agony of protracted trial, spanning over a period of more than 30 years and has been in the corridors of the court for this prolonged period.
In view of the facts noted above, the case of the petitioner deserves to be dealt with leniency.
The petitioner also deserves the benefit of the consistent view taken by this court in this regard.

Thus,
guided by the judicial pronouncements made by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the cases of Panchram vs The State Of Chhattisgarh and Ors reported in AIR 2023 SC 1801 and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, age of petitioner, his status in the society and the fact that he faced financial hardship and had to go through mental agony, this court is of the view that ends of justice would be met, if sentence imposed upon him is reduced to the period already undergone by Mohan Lal vs State on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82421576/
2 him.

sentences.text:
7. Accordingly, the judgment of conviction dated 02.11.2002 passed by the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kapasan, Chittorgarh in Criminal Regular Case No.08/1995 as well as the judgment in appeal dated 28.11.2003 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge No. 2,
Chittorgarh in Criminal appeal No.20/2002 are affirmed but the quantum of sentence awarded by the learned trial court to the petitioner for his (5 of 5) [CRLR-1119/2003] respective offences is modified to the extent that for each count, the sentence undergone by the petitioner till date would be sufficient and justifiable to serve the interest of justice.

He need not surrender.
His bail bonds are discharged.
8. The revision petition is allowed in part.
Pending applications, if any, are disposed of.
9. Record be sent back.
